threats.title: Account Takeover
threats.description: Password guessing, reused passwords, or a fake Shogun sign-in page let someone sign in as another user
threats.mitigation:
Firebase Auth throttles repeated sign-in attempts (provided by Firebase). Offering Google or Apple sign-in avoids passwords. Phishing itself cannot be fully prevented.

CHECK: Phase 2A Step 2 for which sign-in methods and protections are switched on.

threats.title: Server Credentials
threats.description: Stolen server credential lets someone send fake heartbeats or download the member list
threats.mitigation:
Hub stores only a hash; owner can revoke and rotate the credential.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Steps 5-6 (Hub stores only a hash; constant-time comparison; owner-only file permissions on the Server). MISSING: no phase lets an owner revoke or rotate a server credential yet.

threats.title: Squatting
threats.description: Squatting; registering a server ID that belongs to someone else's server
threats.mitigation:
Register refuses an ID that's already claimed.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 6 (claims looked up by ID and registration secret; the ID is hidden from the health endpoint until claimed).

threats.title: Denying Actions
threats.description: Admin or theme author denies an action they took
threats.mitigation:
Functions write an audit log recording the user ID, action, target, and time; clients can't edit it.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 5 (every function logs what happened, without secrets). GAP TO DECIDE: Cloud Logging keeps logs for 30 days by default, and Phase 6 Step 7 has no lasting moderation record.

threats.title: Key Leaks
threats.description: Server-pass signing key leaks, so anyone can forge passes for any server
threats.mitigation:
Key kept in the Secret Manager with only the signing function allowed to read it; key IDs in JWKS so keys can be rotated.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 8 (private key in Secret Manager, readable only by the signing function, never committed; key IDs and a written rotation plan) and Phase 5 Step 7 (production check).

threats.title: Claim Codes
threats.description: Stolen or brute-forced claim code lets an attacker take over someone's server
threats.mitigation:
Claim codes expire quickly, work once, and claim attempts are rate-limited per user.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 6 (claim code stored as a hash, 30-minute expiry, single use) and Step 5 (per-user rate-limit counters).

threats.title: Invite Links
threats.description: Leaked invite link lets a stranger join a server
threats.mitigation:
Invites expire and have a use limit; owner can approve each join and revoke invites.

PLANNED: Phase 6 Step 1 (single-use, expiring, hashed invite tokens; a limit on accept attempts; owner can revoke).

threats.title: Calling Admin Functions
threats.description: A normal user calls the admin moderation functions
threats.mitigation:
Each admin function checks for an admin custom claim on the caller's token.

PLANNED: Phase 6 Step 7 (admin custom claim, checked inside every admin function).

threats.mitigation: N/A: the Admin SDK runs only inside Cloud Functions and never leaves Google's cloud. Threats to the function itself are listed on Hub Functions.

threats.title: Tampering Servers
threats.description: User edits other people's server, invite, or profile documents directly through the SDK
threats.mitigation:
Firestore Security Rules deny client writes to sensitive documents; those writes go only through Hub functions.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 3 (server and membership data written only by Cloud Functions) and Step 4 (Security Rules with allowed and denied tests in CI).

threats.title: Reading Server Info
threats.description: User reads other servers' addresses, invites, or push tokens
threats.mitigation:
Rules allow a server's documents to be read only by its owner and members; push tokens are never readable by clients.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Steps 3-4 (rules limit reads to the owner and members; tested in CI).

threats.title: Info Leak
threats.description: Push notification text shows private info, such as chat messages or server names, on a lock screen
threats.mitigation:
Keep notification text minimal; the app fetches details after the user opens it.

PLANNED: Phase 6 Step 6 (notification says only "New message on <server>"; message text never reaches the Hub).

threats.title: Exposed Credential Hashes
threats.description: A rule mistake exposes serverSecrets, letting someone try to crack server credential hashes
threats.mitigation:
serverSecrets is readable by no app; credentials are long random values, so their hashes cannot be cracked.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 3 (serverSecrets readable by no app) and Step 4 (a denied-read test).

threats.title: Filling Storage
threats.description: Someone uploads many or very large files to fill storage and raise the bill
threats.mitigation:
Storage rules limit file type and size; budget alerts catch unusual cost.

PLANNED: Phase 6 (Cloud Storage Security Rules) and Phase 2A Step 1 (budget alerts).

threats.title: Fake Public Keys
threats.description: Server is tricked into trusting fake public keys
threats.mitigation:
JWKS URL build into the Server, HTTPs only, keys cached.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 8 (JWKS and OpenID configuration at a stable HTTPS address on Hosting) and Step 10 (the Server is configured with the Hub as issuer).

threats.title: Malicious Themes
threats.description: Malicious themes carries script, CSS, or SVG that runs in other users' browsers
threats.mitigation:
Themes are data only (JSON); a function checks them against a schema; Storage rules limit file type (no SVG) and size.

PLANNED: Phase 6 Step 9 (theme JSON Schema checked in the web app, Cloud Functions, and the Server; unknown fields rejected), Step 11 (review queue), and Cloud Storage Security Rules.

threats.title: Spam Calls
threats.description: Spam calls or uploads run up the Firebase bill
threats.mitigation:
App Check, per-user rate limits, Storage size limits, and budget alerts.

PLANNED: Phase 2A Step 1 (budget with email alerts), Step 5 (rate-limit counters), and Phase 5 Steps 7 and 13 (App Check, enforced).
